messages:
maya: quick heads-up — p99s on host-side tokenization spiked ~15% after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak
ajay: ugh. saw that in dashboards. is it steady or only on long seqs?
maya: mostly for seq>1024 and when streaming chunk size > 8kb. repro with the small loadtest I pushed to ci-perf
lee: can you drop the perf trace link? want to inspect stacks
maya: https://perf.internal/trace/1791122334
maya: trace shows heavy time in HostTokenizer::emit_chunks and in grpc::Writev (lots of tiny writes)
serena: thought kernel selector change only touched GPU path. how does that affect host tokenization?
ajay: it changes batching heuristics — we now pack more small requests into one kernel call which changed arrival patterns at host preproc
lee: so kv cache warmup timing shifted, more cache misses leading to extra parse work?
maya: exactly — kvcache miss rate up ~3.2% at the spike window, causing extra KV restore reads and extra prefix re-tokenize
perf-bot: autotriage: regression likely due to batching-policy v2. Repro prob 85% on long sequences
maya: I tried toggling batching_policy=legacy in local and p99 drops back to baseline
ajay: can we short-circuit tokenization for already-cached prefixes? maybe a header flag from runtime to skip pre-tokenization
lee: also grpc small-writes are killing us. need to coalesce streaming chunks into fewer writev calls. current shim emits one chunk per token group
maya: quick patch I tested: bundle up to 32kb before writev and add backpressure on the encoder flush. p99 down 7% in canary
serena: sounds promising. what's the tradeoff on tail latency for tiny requests?
maya: tiny requests (<=8 tokens) see +0.5ms median; overall cost saving probably worth it for our workload mix
ajay: kernel selection heuristic tweak: prefer smaller batch kernel when more than 60% requests are short. that avoided kv thrash in my local
lee: we should add a perf regression test that simulates mixed seqs and measures kv miss/donwstream parse time. open a PR with script
maya: filed a draft PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4321 — includes trace, microbench, and canary config
deploy-bot: canary rolled out to 3 pods with bundling patch @eng-runtime — observing metrics
serena: schedule a short sync to decide rollout? 30min?
ajay: 30 works for me. I'll bring charts and the kv-hit-rate flamegraph
lee: I'll bring a list of mitigations: token-cache fast-path, writev coalescer, batching-policy rollback toggle
maya: thanks — see you in 30. :thumbsup:
